\section{Fixed points}
A fixed point of a map $f$ satisfies $f(x^*)=x^*$.
Linear stability depends on the derivative $f'(x^*)$.
\subsection{Example}
Consider the logistic map $x_{n+1}=r x_n(1-x_n)$ near a fixed point.
When $|f'(x^*)|<1$ the fixed point is attracting.
\section{Feedback}
Negative feedback can stabilise a complex system around an operating point.
Positive feedback amplifies small perturbations.
